### Page note: https://butterfly-conservation.org/our-work/recording-and-monitoring/big-butterfly-count/big-butterfly-count-2015-results
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
**Page:** Big Butterfly Count 2015 results – https://butterfly-conservation.org/our-work/recording-and-monitoring/big-butterfly-count/big-butterfly-count-2015-results  

**Evidence**  
- “**Gatekeeper** 106 995 **17**”  
- “**Large White** 83 042 **46**”  
- “**Meadow Brown** 76 713 **16**”  
- “**Small White** 72 483 **-3**”  
- “**Peacock** 42 754 **-61**”  
- “**Small Tortoiseshell** 31 322 **-57**”  
- “**Ringlet** 27 604 **75**”  
- “**Red Admiral** 21 027 **-28**”  
- “**Comma** 18 765 **42**”  
- “**Common Blue** 17 932 **-12**”  
- “**Green‑veined White** 14 437 **-42**”  
- “**Speckled Wood** 12 342 **-25**”  
- “**Large Skipper** 11 198 **24**”  
- “**Holly Blue** 10 334 **151**”  
- “**Six‑spot Burnet** 9 448 **2**”  
- “**Marbled White** 8 071 **52**”  
- “**Painted Lady** 7 416 **28**”  
- “**Brimstone** 6 075 **18**”  
- “**Small Copper** 4 395 **-28**”  
- “**Silver Y** 1 912 **92**”  
  *(These are the 20 rows of the “Abundance % change from 2014” table.)*  

- “The biggest increase was achieved by the **Holly Blue** (151 % increase on 2014)” – narrative confirmation of the table value.  
- “**Gatekeeper** numbers only increased modestly (up 17 % on last year)” – narrative confirmation.  
- “**Painted Lady** also had a good year (numbers up 28 % on 2014)” – narrative confirmation.  
- “**Large White** … numbers up by 46 %” – narrative confirmation.  
- “**Ringlet** achieved its second highest position …, 2nd‑highest position in 2015” – narrative context.  
- “The 2015 period (17 July ‑ 9 August) … almost 585 000 individual butterflies and moths of the 20 target species were counted and logged online.”  
- “The average number of individual butterflies seen per count decreased from 15 last year to 13 this year (a 9 % decrease).”  
- “Over 52 000 people took part in the 2015 event.”  

**Coverage**  
- The page provides a full list of all 20 target species for the 2015 Big Butterfly Count, each paired with its numeric abundance and the percentage change from the previous year (2014).  
- Covers the entire 2015 event (17 July ‑ 9 August) and nationwide totals for participants and insect counts.  
- The data is specifically for 2015; no 2017 information is present.  

**Missing**  
- Percentage change data for each species in 2017 (relative to 2016).  
- Any 2015 data for species not in the top 20 (none exist – all 20 target species are listed).  
- Confirmation of 2015 figures relative to 2014 beyond the provided table (the table is the only source).  

**Next links**  
- https://butterfly-conservation.org/our-work/recording-and-monitoring/big-butterfly-count/big-butterfly-count-2017-results – could provide the 2017 species‑level % change data needed for the question.

### Page note: https://butterfly-conservation.org/our-work/recording-and-monitoring/big-butterfly-count/big-butterfly-count-2017-results
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
**Page:** Big Butterfly Count 2017 results – https://butterfly-conservation.org/our-work/recording-and-monitoring/big-butterfly-count/big-butterfly-count-2017-results  

**Evidence**  
- Overall 2017 results summary  
  - “Despite an amazing **550,000** individual insects of the 20 target species being spotted during **big butterfly count 2017**.”  
  - “The average number of individuals seen per 15 minute count was the lowest recorded since the project began in 2010 – **10.9** individuals per count, down from **12.2** in 2016.”  
  - “Altogether, **62,547** counts were submitted by over **60,400** participants, a **64 %** increase in the number of counts and a **66 %** increase in the number of people taking part compared with 2016.”  

- 2017 species‑rank / percent‑change table (abundance change from 2016)  
  | Rank | Species | 2017 count | 2016 count | % change (2017 vs 2016) |  
  |------|---------|------------|------------|------------------------|  
  | 1 | Gatekeeper | 931 | 171 | **+24 %** |  
  | 2 | Red Admiral | 731 | 161 | **+75 %** |  
  | 3 | Meadow Brown | 695 | 28 | **‑23 %** |  
  | 4 | Small White | 618 | 12 | **‑37 %** |  
  | 5 | Large White | 610 | 64 | **‑38 %** |  
  | 6 | Peacock | 294 | 54 | **+1 %** |  
  | 7 | Comma | 224 | 36 | **+90 %** |  
  | 8 | Small Tortoiseshell | 202 | 67 | **+4 %** |  
  | 9 | Common Blue | 195 | 67 | **+109 %** |  
  |10 | Speckled Wood | 186 | 39 | **+15 %** |  
  |11 | Ringlet | 183 | 81 | **‑57 %** |  
  |12 | Green‑veined White | 164 | 56 | **‑38 %** |  
  |13 | Six‑spot Burnet | 95 | 7 | **‑28 %** |  
  |14 | Painted Lady | 87 | 37 | **+31 %** |  
  |15 | Large Skipper | 65 | 79 | **‑49 %** |  
  |16 | Holly Blue | 59 | 29 | **‑5 %** |  
  |17 | Small Copper | 58 | 14 | **+62 %** |  
  |18 | Brimstone | 52 | 81 | **‑7 %** |  
  |19 | Marbled White | 48 | 94 | **‑67 %** |  
  |20 | Silver Y | 19 | 23 | **‑2 %** |  

- Additional specific species insights quoted in text  
  - “Red Admiral… numbers… up **75 %** compared with the 2016 Count and threefold compared with 2015.”  
  - “Comma… up by **90 %** from a relatively poor year in 2016.”  
  - “Common Blue… up **109 %** (2017) and **62 %** (2016).”  
  - “Small Copper… strong increase of **62 %**.”  

**Coverage**  
- Entities: 20 target butterfly species (listed in the table).  
- Years: 2016 (as reference) and 2017 (primary data).  
- Conditions: ‘Abundance % change from 2016’ – relative changes between contiguous years.  
- Units: counts (raw totals per species for the whole count period) and percentages (change relative to previous year).  
- The table provides **all 20 species**; thus the list is **complete** for 2017 abundance changes relative to 2016.  
- The overall metrics (total insects, average per 15 min, counts, participants, percentage increases) cover the entire 2017 count event.  

**Missing**  
- Any data on percentage changes for 2015 versus 2014 (required to assess 2015 change).  
- Column of 2015 counts and % change from 2014 (or from 2015 relative to 2014).  
- Direct link or table giving the 2015 abundance changes needed to compare against 2017.  
- The species list of those with ≥20 % change in both 2015 and 2017 cannot be derived from this page.  

**Next links**  
1. **Big Butterfly Count 2015 results** – likely at  
   `https://butterfly-conservation.org/our-work/recording-and-monitoring/big-butterfly-count/big-butterfly-count-2015-results`  
   *Missing field:* 2015 species abundance and % change table, needed to check which species had ≥20 % change in 2015.  

2. **Big Butterfly Count 2015 Country results** (under “Big Butterfly Count 2017 Country results”) – may provide regional data, not directly needed.
